author: elder
title: Same-calibration DAY-EFFECT pairs — decoded, and the identifying assumption is NOT supported
decoder: FWHT — decoder of record per adopted Item 1; 15.6 s per n=14 arm

P_recovery_validity_check.note: P is public and re-used BY DESIGN (P-controlled); recovering it validates the flight, it does not identify anything

prereg_verdicts.SIGNIFICANCE: the two pairs return DIFFERENT verdicts — that divergence IS the result

identifying_assumption_test.VERDICT: 1.91 sigma — BELOW the pre-registered 2-sigma bar, but the observed effect is 93% of the smallest this design can resolve. This is NOT a null; it is an underpowered test landing a hair below its own resolution. Required phrasing: 'no day-dependence larger than 0.0825 detected (96% of the n-effect)' — NOT 'the assumption was verified'.

what_looks_solid.reading: the MEAN n-effect reproduces well; it is the VARIANCE ACROSS CALIBRATIONS that is large
what_looks_solid.H1_supported: per-flight variation is real and large — which is precisely what makes H2 vs H3 unresolvable from two pairs

CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_LADDER: the n=14 outlier CANNOT be attributed. Pair 1 reproduces it HIGHER (retention 0.6105) and pair 2 lands almost exactly on it (0.5584). One pair says the high value is real, the other says it was ordinary. Two pairs sufficed to show the assumption is shaky and NOT to resolve what it hides — the outcome the power table predicted at 62 QPU-s.
recommendation: do NOT size rung 15 off a point estimate from a curve whose per-flight variance is this large. Either fly a third pair (~31 QPU-s, marginal value now HIGH because the estimate sits AT the resolution limit) or size with an explicit per-flight error term.
